newsitem.title: USA: First Union expects to meet '96 EPS target.
newsitem.headline: First Union expects to meet '96 EPS target.

text.p: First Union Corp Chairman Ed Crutchfield said on Thursday the bank was on target to earn $6.31 a share this year.

Although the $5.4 billion purchase of First Fidelity Bancorp, completed in January, had a slight impact on First Union's first-quarter results, higher fees from non-traditional banking products have enabled it to stay on target, Crutchfield told Reuters during a telephone interview.
The acquisition turned First Union into the sixth-largest U.S. bank and added northern customers -- from Connecticut to Pennsylvania -- to its East Coast base that stretches to Key West, Fla.
Crutchfield said the bank had completed technology conversions and the introduction of First Union products in the First Fidelity network, which is now called First Union-North.
Indeed, First Union's CAP account, which combines traditional banking and investments, has become the leading consumer product in the expanded market.
